name: Taroudant Ramparts
hero_subtitle: Kilometres of ochre walls and gates — the silhouette that defines Taroudant.

info.entry_val: Free for exterior walks; certain sections vary

overview.title: The Walls That Earned the Nickname
overview.p1: Taroudant’s ochre mudbrick ramparts wrap completely around the town. It is why travellers call it the Little Marrakech of the Souss — a fortified layout without the imperial city crowds.
overview.p2: Walk outside the walls for classic views, pause at the monumental gates, and catch the late light when the earth glows. Pick a scenic section rather than walking the full loop in the heat.

moods.title: The Ramparts Through the Day
moods.subtitle: Shade is limited — light and heat set your distance.

1.title: Cooler Circuit
1.desc: Mornings are gentler for longer stretches outside the walls.

2.title: Harsh Exposure
2.desc: Midday is exhausting on open ground; keep walks short.

3.title: Golden Ochre
3.desc: Late light offers the classic photo moment on the mudbrick.

food.title: Eating Near the Ramparts
food.p1: There are no restaurants on the ramparts themselves. Head back into the medina or Place Assarag for cafés and tagines.
food.p2: Carry water; plan your meals inside the town centre.
food.li2: Cafés near the main gates and Place Assarag.
food.li4: A hat and sunscreen are essential.
food.li5: Do not rely on stalls along the walls.

1.title: How Far to Walk
1.desc: The full loop is long. Pick one scenic section and a gate instead of doing the whole circuit.

2.title: Footwear
2.desc: Dusty, uneven ground outside the walls — closed-toe shoes help.

3.title: Sunset
3.desc: Arrive before sunset for the richest colour on the ochre earth.

q1.question: Can I walk on top of the ramparts?
q1.answer: Access varies by section; most visitors walk along the outside for the best views.

q2.question: How long is the full circuit?
q2.answer: Several kilometres — plan a short section rather than a full loop in summer heat.

q3.question: Which gate is best to start at?
q3.answer: Ask your hotel or riad for the nearest scenic section and main gate.

q4.question: Are they suitable for families?
q4.answer: Yes, for short stretches combined with shaded breaks inside the medina.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required for an exterior walk, though helpful if you want the history of the gates.
